task: When a declared LiteLLM auto-router has no positive max_output_tokens, LLMService sets it at catalog load to the smallest positive max_output_tokens among its distinct tier models; it stays unset and a warning is logged when any tier is unresolved or has no positive limit; an explicit router value wins (EPMCDME-16835).

key_reasoning.reason: The only production change is in LLMService: a module helper _is_positive_limit, the static method _router_max_output_tokens (a near copy of the existing _router_max_input_tokens: distinct tier names, minimum, None when any tier is unknown) and _apply_router_output_limits, called once at the start of initialize_default_litellm_models. llm_factory forwarding is unchanged and LLM_PROXY_FORWARD_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS still turns forwarding off. Residual risks are small: the catalog LLMModel objects are changed in place at load, the bool/zero/negative guards matter because a value above any tier's own limit would make the provider reject the request, and per-user catalogs from get_user_allowed_models do not go through initialize_default_litellm_models, so they do not get a derived limit. Rollback means reverting one call.

3 files modified, 0 new (276 insertions, 2 deletions). Only one is a source file (+45 lines in service/llm_service). The other two are tests: test_llm_service_litellm_integration.py (+175) and tests/enterprise/litellm/test_llm_factory.py (+58, catalog-to-max_tokens forwarding end to end). The changes span 3 directories, but 2 of them hold only tests, so this stays at S.

The plan left two policy choices open. The implementation settled both: return None for unresolved tiers, as the max_input_tokens precedent does, and log the derivation. This is a small clarification cost, consistent with S.
